literature_scope.role: Assignment-design / exposure-mapping / estimand separation (Aronow-Samii); rerandomization as conditioning on a pre-treatment balance event (Morgan-Rubin); exact rejective-sampling law q_B(A)=q(A)1{B(A)}/P_q(B) (Hájek). None of these titles is imported as a project theorem verbatim.
limitations: Task-1 design/exposure labels and their 4-feature extensions are not source taxonomies.
The project's exact full-assignment enumeration (N<=8) is not the source papers' asymptotic theory.
Exposure sufficiency is NOT a condition for the design-standardized arm mean; it is a separate interpretation upgrade.

identification_statement.identified: Design-standardized conditional arm mean mu_i^q(a,s)=E[Y_i^obs | T_i=a, S_i=s] whenever pi_i(a,s)>0; direct/spillover effects are contrasts of these arm means; fixed-policy value and two-policy difference are identified under the known full assignment law (R1B) or, when mean-signature sufficiency is explicitly adopted, via the mean-signature route (R2). Features ① unequal fixed quota, ② rerandomization, ③ weighted exposure, ④ grouped exposure are all wired to the single-arm, batch, composition and business-dispatch paths (D1-D8), and both R1B and R2 reach the new designs.
conditions: task-1 exact support uses full-assignment enumeration, N<=8
identification_statement.exposure_sufficiency_note: exposure_sufficiency is NOT required for the design-standardized contrast; adopting it only upgrades the interpretation to a causal effect of exposure (recorded as interpretation=causal_effect_under_exposure_sufficiency vs design_standardized_contrast).
not_yet_supported: analytic conditional count law for N>8 task-1 designs
numeric PFN estimation (task requires identification only)
R2 mean-signature sufficiency for weighted/grouped exposures (R2 is an E1-E5 signature route; W/G uses R1B/effect routes)
independent assignment-mass recomputation for weighted/grouped exposure on D4-D6 (exposure statistic is independent; mass still mirrors the declared full law)
dispatcher does not prefer R2 when both R1B and R2 are available (R2 is planned and independently executable, but the existing first-success selection returns R1B)
arbitrary stochastic policy kernels, dynamic/unknown graphs, multi-valued or continuous treatment, R3 observational conditional decomposition

verification_evidence: Documentation, implementation and test pointers checked against the current source; Task-1 native/composition/business-dispatch tests pass, and the D1-D8 x E1-E5 x four-family reference passes 160/160. No new theorem imported from the cited literature; the project derivation is independent.
